question: Indian Navy Sailing Championship 2022, one of the events being conducted by the Indian Navy to commemorate Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav and khelo India, was held in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Navy Sailing Championship (INSC) 2022 was conducted by the Indian Naval Academy, Ezhimala, in Kerala, as part of the events commemorating Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav and promoting Khelo India. (भारतीय नौसेना नौकायन चैंपियनशिप 2022 — केरल)

 

• The championship brought together sailors from across the Indian Navy to compete in various sailing classes, encouraging the sport of sailing among service personnel.

 

• It was organised under the aegis of the Indian Naval Sailing Association (INSA), which promotes competitive and adventure sailing in the Navy.

 

• Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav is the Government of India's initiative to celebrate 75 years of independence, under which the Navy also conducted events like the Kochi-to-Goa offshore sailing regatta.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Naval Academy (INA) at Ezhimala, Kerala, is the largest naval academy in Asia and trains officers for the Indian Navy and Coast Guard.

 

• Khelo India is a national programme launched in 2018 to revive sports culture in India through infrastructure and talent development.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 1): Not the venue; associated instead with naval facilities like INS Dega, Visakhapatnam, but not this championship.

 

• West Bengal (Option 2): Not connected with this event.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Not connected with this event; Tamil Nadu hosts other naval training establishments like INS Adyar.

question: Ramesh Bais served as Governor in which of the following states before being appointed as Governor of Maharashtra in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ramesh Bais served as the Governor of Jharkhand from 2021 until he was appointed Governor of Maharashtra in February 2023. (रमेश बैस — झारखंड के राज्यपाल)

 

• Before Jharkhand, he had earlier served as the Governor of Tripura (2019-2021).

 

• As Governor of Maharashtra, he succeeded Bhagat Singh Koshyari.

 

• Ramesh Bais is a veteran BJP leader from Chhattisgarh who has also held union ministerial positions before moving into gubernatorial roles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Governors are appointed by the President of India under Article 155 of the Constitution and hold office during the pleasure of the President as per Article 156.

 

• A Governor can be transferred from one state to another, as seen in Ramesh Bais's career progression through Tripura, Jharkhand, and Maharashtra.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1): Ramesh Bais did not serve as Governor of Odisha; Odisha's Governor at the time was Ganeshi Lal, later succeeded by Raghubar Das.

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): He did not serve as Governor of Karnataka.

 

• West Bengal (Option 4): He did not serve as Governor of West Bengal.

question: In which year did Niels Bohr propose a theory for the hydrogen atom based on the quantum theory that some physical quantities take only discrete values?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1913.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1913, the Danish physicist Niels Bohr proposed the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, applying quantum theory to explain that electrons orbit the nucleus only in certain discrete, quantised energy levels. (नील्स बोर — 1913, बोर परमाणु मॉडल)

 

• This model explained the hydrogen emission spectrum and introduced the idea that electrons could jump between fixed orbits by absorbing or emitting a quantum of energy (a photon).

 

• Bohr's model built on Rutherford's nuclear model of the atom (1911) and Planck's quantum theory, and was a major step towards modern quantum mechanics.

 

• For this and related work, Niels Bohr was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1922.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ernest Rutherford proposed the nuclear model of the atom in 1911, which Bohr's theory refined.

 

• The Bohr model was later superseded by the more complete quantum mechanical model developed by Schrodinger, Heisenberg and others in the 1920s.

 

NOTE

 

• 1919 (Option 1): Not the year of Bohr's theory; in 1919 Rutherford discovered the proton.

 

• 1921 (Option 2): Not the correct year for this proposal.

 

• 1909 (Option 3): This predates both Rutherford's nuclear model (1911) and Bohr's theory (1913), so it is incorrect.

question: Which d-block element in the periodic table is represented by the Greek symbol 'alpha' and the metallic 'rays'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Actinium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Actinium (symbol Ac, atomic number 89) derives its name from the Greek word "aktinos" (or "aktis"), meaning "ray" or "beam", referring to the radioactive rays it emits. (एक्टिनियम — किरण)

 

• It was discovered in 1899 by Andre-Louis Debierne, a French chemist, while working with pitchblende residues.

 

• Actinium heads the actinide series and is placed in Group 3 of the periodic table, which is treated as part of the d-block in many periodic table representations.

 

• It is a silvery-white, highly radioactive metal that glows in the dark due to its intense radioactivity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The actinide series (Actinium to Lawrencium) consists of 15 elements, most of which are synthetic and radioactive.

 

• Elements named similarly for their radiant/ray-like properties include Radium (from Latin "radius", meaning ray).

 

NOTE

 

• Lanthanum (Option 1): Heads the lanthanide series; its name comes from the Greek "lanthanein", meaning "to lie hidden", not "ray".

 

• Rhenium (Option 3): A d-block transition metal named after the river Rhine, not related to "rays".

 

• Tungsten (Option 4): A d-block metal whose name comes from Swedish "tung sten" meaning "heavy stone".

question: Who among the following organised Sarvajanik Ganesh Utsav to inculcate national sentiments among the masses?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lokmanya Tilak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Lokmanya Tilak) started the Sarvajanik Ganesh Utsav (public Ganesh festival) in 1893 in Pune to unite people across castes and communities and inculcate national and political consciousness under the guise of a religious festival. (बाल गंगाधर तिलक — सार्वजनिक गणेशोत्सव)

 

• Since public political gatherings were restricted by the British, Tilak used the religious festival platform to bring people together and spread nationalist ideas.

 

• Tilak also popularised the Shivaji Jayanti festival for similar purposes, celebrating the legacy of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

 

• He is famously known for the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tilak was one of the trio known as "Lal-Bal-Pal" (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal), leaders of the extremist/assertive nationalist phase of the freedom movement.

 

• Tilak also authored "Gita Rahasya" and edited the newspapers Kesari and Mahratta.

 

NOTE

 

• Bipin Chandra Pal (Option 2): A prominent nationalist leader and part of the "Lal-Bal-Pal" trio, but not the founder of the Sarvajanik Ganesh Utsav.

 

• Aurobindo Ghosh (Option 3): A revolutionary nationalist and later spiritual philosopher, not associated with founding this festival.

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai (Option 4): Known as "Punjab Kesari", part of the "Lal-Bal-Pal" trio, but did not start the Sarvajanik Ganesh Utsav.

question: Which event was hosted at Lord's Cricket Ground(LCG) at the 2012 Olympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Archery.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2012 Summer Olympics in London, the Archery events were hosted at the historic Lord's Cricket Ground, home of English and world cricket. (लॉर्ड्स क्रिकेट ग्राउंड — तीरंदाजी, लंदन ओलंपिक 2012)

 

• A temporary archery field, the "Lord's Cricket Ground venue", was set up within the ground specifically for the Olympic archery competition.

 

• Cricket itself has never been an Olympic sport (except for a single appearance at the 1900 Paris Games), so it was not played at the 2012 Olympics.

 

• Using such an iconic, non-traditional Olympic venue reflected London 2012's approach of hosting events at recognisable heritage sites across the city.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Boxing at London 2012 was held at the ExCeL London exhibition centre.

 

• Equestrian events were held at Greenwich Park, another iconic heritage venue used for the 2012 Games.

 

NOTE

 

• Boxing (Option 1): Held at ExCeL London, not Lord's.

 

• Cricket (Option 2): Not an Olympic sport in 2012; hence not hosted anywhere at the Games.

 

• Equestrian (Option 4): Held at Greenwich Park, not Lord's Cricket Ground.

question: Which of the following is the compelling factor that produced a very high repayment rate of 98% in the concept of lending to groups of poor women, initiated by Dr Yunus?
option_2: Removal of the defaulter from the group
option_3: Joint liability putting social pressure to repay loans
option_4: Use of the services of aggressive loan recovery agents
solution_text:
The correct answer is Joint liability putting social pressure to repay loans.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr Muhammad Yunus, founder of the Grameen Bank in Bangladesh, pioneered group-based microcredit lending to poor women, using the concept of joint liability, where each member of the small group is collectively responsible for the loans of others. (मुहम्मद यूनुस — ग्रामीण बैंक, संयुक्त दायित्व)

 

• This joint liability creates peer/social pressure within the group to ensure timely repayment, since a default by one member can affect the creditworthiness and future borrowing of the whole group.

 

• This mechanism, rather than collateral, was the key innovation that produced repayment rates as high as 98% in the Grameen Bank model.

 

• For this work, Dr Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank jointly won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Grameen Bank was formally established in 1983 and primarily provides collateral-free microloans to the rural poor, especially women.

 

• This model inspired the global microfinance movement, including Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Involvement of ‘loan sharks’ (Option 1): Loan sharks charge exploitative interest and are the opposite of what microfinance seeks to replace.

 

• Removal of the defaulter from the group (Option 2): Not the mechanism used; the model relies on collective responsibility, not expulsion.

 

• Use of the services of aggressive loan recovery agents (Option 4): Not used by Grameen Bank; its model relies on peer pressure and trust, not coercive recovery.

question: Which of the following forest types is found on the foothills of the Himalayas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Deciduous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The foothills of the Himalayas (the Shivalik and Terai belt) fall in the tropical/subtropical zone and support moist and dry deciduous forests, where trees shed their leaves in a particular season. (हिमालय की तलहटी — पर्णपाती वन)

 

• As altitude increases up the Himalayas, forest types change in a clear vertical zonation: tropical deciduous (foothills) -> subtropical -> temperate -> alpine -> tundra (near the snowline).

 

• Common trees of these foothill deciduous forests include Sal, Sheesham and Khair.

 

• This altitudinal zonation of vegetation in the Himalayas is a classic example of how climate changes with elevation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Temperate forests occur at middle elevations (roughly 1,500-3,000 m) in the Himalayas.

 

• Alpine vegetation (shrubs, grasses) occurs above the temperate zone, just below the permanent snowline, while tundra-like vegetation occurs at the highest, coldest elevations.

 

NOTE

 

• Temperate (Option 1): Found at higher elevations than the foothills, not at the base.

 

• Tundra (Option 2): Found at very high elevations near the snowline, not the foothills.

 

• Alpine (Option 3): Found above the temperate zone at high altitudes, not at the foothills.

question: What is the Crude Death Rate of India as per Census 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.1%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census/Sample Registration System (SRS) data, the Crude Death Rate (CDR) of India stood at 7.1 (deaths per 1,000 population per year). (भारत की मृत्यु दर — 7.1, जनगणना 2011)

 

• Crude Death Rate is defined as the number of deaths occurring during a year per 1,000 of the estimated mid-year population of that area.

 

• India's CDR has been steadily declining over the decades due to improvements in healthcare, sanitation and nutrition, from around 25 in 1951 to about 7 by 2011.

 

• The corresponding Crude Birth Rate (CBR) as per the same period was around 21.8 per 1,000 population.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• CDR is one of the key demographic indicators used alongside CBR (Crude Birth Rate) and IMR (Infant Mortality Rate) to assess a country's health and development status.

 

• The Registrar General of India (RGI) conducts the Sample Registration System (SRS) which provides annual vital statistics like CDR, CBR and IMR.

 

NOTE

 

• 10% (Option 1): Far higher than India's actual CDR figures around the 2011 Census period.

 

• 8.5% (Option 2): Close to, but not matching, the accepted 2011 figure of 7.1.

 

• 5.9% (Option 3): Lower than the accepted figure for that period.

question: Which of the following presents awards and recognitions in the field of Indian dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, established in 1952, confers awards and fellowships (Akademi Puraskar and Akademi Ratna/Fellowship) in recognition of excellence in the performing arts, including classical and folk dance. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी — नृत्य पुरस्कार)

 

• It is the oldest of the National Akademis set up by the Government of India, headquartered in New Delhi.

 

• It plays a key role in the preservation and promotion of India's diverse dance and music traditions and administers institutions like Kathak Kendra.

 

• Its awards are among the highest official recognitions for performing artists in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sahitya Akademi is India's national academy of letters, promoting literature.

 

• Lalit Kala Akademi is the national academy for visual/fine arts such as painting and sculpture.

 

NOTE

 

• INTACH (Option 1): The Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage works for heritage conservation, not dance awards.

 

• Sahitya Akademi (Option 3): Focuses on literature, not dance.

 

• Lalit Kala Akademi (Option 4): Focuses on visual arts, not performing arts like dance.

question: Who among the following Indian cricketers has won the ICC Emerging Women’s cricketer award for the year 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Renuka Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Renuka Singh (Thakur), the Indian pace bowler, was named the ICC Women's Emerging Cricketer of the Year for 2022. (रेणुका सिंह — ICC इमर्जिंग महिला क्रिकेटर 2022)

 

• She was recognised for her impressive performances with the ball for the Indian women's cricket team during the award period.

 

• This award is part of the annual ICC Awards, which recognise the best performers in international cricket across various categories.

 

• Renuka Singh hails from Himachal Pradesh and has been a key fast bowler for India in white-ball cricket.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The men's counterpart award for 2022, ICC Men's Emerging Cricketer of the Year, was won by a different player; such awards recognise young/upcoming talent.

 

• Smriti Mandhana has won the ICC Women's ODI Cricketer of the Year award in other years, a separate category from the Emerging Cricketer award.

 

NOTE

 

• Smriti Mandhana (Option 1): A senior established India batter, not the 2022 Emerging Cricketer awardee.

 

• Harmanpreet Kaur (Option 3): India's senior women's team captain, not eligible/awarded in the emerging category for 2022.

 

• Jhulan Goswami (Option 4): A veteran India pacer nearing retirement in 2022, not an "emerging" player.

question: Alvars were the devotees of which South Indian cult?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vaishnavism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Alvars were a group of twelve Tamil poet-saints (circa 6th-9th century CE) who were devout worshippers of Lord Vishnu, composing devotional hymns in praise of Vishnu and his incarnations. (आलवार संत — वैष्णव भक्ति)

 

• Their devotional compositions were later compiled into the "Naalayira Divya Prabandham" (Four Thousand Divine Verses), a foundational text of Tamil Vaishnava Bhakti literature.

 

• The Alvars, along with the Nayanars (Shaivite saints), were central to the Bhakti movement in South India, spreading devotional worship among the masses in the vernacular Tamil language rather than Sanskrit.

 

• Notable Alvars include Andal (the only female Alvar), Nammalvar, and Periyalvar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nayanars, numbering 63, were the Shaivite counterparts of the Alvars, devoted to Lord Shiva.

 

• The Bhakti movement in South India significantly influenced the later Bhakti movements across northern and eastern India.

 

NOTE

 

• Shaktism (Option 1): Worship of the Divine Mother/Shakti; not associated with the Alvars.

 

• Saivism (Option 2): Worship of Lord Shiva; this was the tradition of the Nayanars, not the Alvars.

 

• Jainism (Option 3): An entirely separate religious tradition, unrelated to the Alvars' Vaishnava devotion.

question: The working conditions also include prevention of sexual harassment of working women and making arrangements in the organisation for it, this falls under ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 42.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 42 of the Indian Constitution, a Directive Principle of State Policy, directs the State to make provision for "just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief". (अनुच्छेद 42 — कार्य की न्यायसंगत एवं मानवोचित दशाएं)

 

• The Supreme Court, in the landmark Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) judgment, laid down the "Vishaka Guidelines" for prevention of sexual harassment of women at the workplace, grounding them in Articles 14, 15, 19, 21 and Article 42 of the Constitution.

 

• These guidelines eventually led to the enactment of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.

 

• "Just and humane conditions of work" is interpreted to include a safe, harassment-free working environment for women.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) are contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution and are non-justiciable but fundamental in governance.

 

• Other labour/welfare-related DPSPs include Article 43 (living wage) and Article 41 (right to work, education and public assistance).

 

NOTE

 

• Article 44 (Option 1): Relates to a Uniform Civil Code, unrelated to workplace conditions.

 

• Article 45 (Option 3): Relates to early childhood care and education for children below 6 years.

 

• Article 43 (Option 4): Relates to securing a living wage and decent standard of life for workers, a related but distinct provision.

question: Which of the following is true about the Zaid season in Indian agriculture?
option_3: It begins with the onset of winter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It follows the Rabi season.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Zaid season is a short cropping season in India that occurs between the Rabi and Kharif seasons, roughly from March to June, i.e., it directly follows the Rabi season. (जायद फसल — रबी के बाद, ग्रीष्मकालीन मौसम)

 

• Since it falls in the hot summer months, Zaid crops are largely irrigation-dependent rather than rainfall-dependent.

 

• Common Zaid crops include watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables and fodder crops.

 

• The three main cropping seasons of India are, in order: Kharif (monsoon, June-October) -> Rabi (winter, October-March) -> Zaid (summer, March-June).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kharif season coincides with the southwest monsoon (June-October) and includes crops like rice, maize, cotton and sugarcane.

 

• The Rabi season begins with the onset of winter (October-November) and includes crops like wheat, mustard, and gram.

 

NOTE

 

• It coincides with southwest monsoon (Option 2): This describes the Kharif season, not Zaid.

 

• It begins with the onset of winter (Option 3): This describes the Rabi season, not Zaid.

 

• It follows the Kharif season (Option 4): It is actually the Rabi season that follows Kharif; Zaid follows Rabi.

question: Talat Aziz is primarily a ______ singer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghazal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Talat Aziz is a renowned Indian Ghazal singer, celebrated for his contribution to popularising the Ghazal genre in India through both live performances and Bollywood playback singing. (तलत अज़ीज़ — गज़ल गायक)

 

• He trained under the legendary Ghazal maestro Ustad Mehdi Hassan, which shaped his distinctive Ghazal singing style.

 

• He has performed and recorded numerous Ghazal albums and has also sung playback for several Hindi films.

 

• Ghazal is a form of amatory poem/song of Persian/Urdu origin, popular in South Asian classical and semi-classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous Ghazal singers of India include Jagjit Singh, Pankaj Udhas and Ustad Ghulam Ali (Pakistan).

 

• Ghazal singing blends elements of Hindustani classical music with Urdu/Persian poetic traditions but is treated as a distinct semi-classical genre.

 

NOTE

 

• Hindustani Classical (Option 1): Talat Aziz is not primarily known as a Hindustani classical vocalist.

 

• Carnatic Classical (Option 2): Carnatic music is a South Indian classical tradition, unrelated to Talat Aziz.

 

• Folk (Option 4): Talat Aziz is not primarily identified as a folk singer.

question: Tevitichiyattam, Nangai Natakam and Dasiyattam are the forms of which of the following classical dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tevitichiyattam, Nangai Natakam and Dasiyattam are older/regional names historically associated with the forms that evolved into Mohiniyattam, the classical dance of Kerala. (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल का शास्त्रीय नृत्य)

 

• Mohiniyattam, meaning "dance of the enchantress", is a graceful, lyrical solo dance form traditionally performed by women.

 

• It draws its themes largely from Vaishnavite traditions and is characterised by swaying body movements and delicate gestures.

 

• Along with Kathakali, Mohiniyattam is one of Kerala's principal classical dance forms, and it is one of the eight classical dance forms of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight classical dances of India are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.

 

• Kathakali, also from Kerala, is a highly stylised dance-drama with elaborate costumes and makeup, distinct from Mohiniyattam.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi dance (Option 1): The classical dance of Odisha, unrelated to these regional Kerala names.

 

• Kathakali dance (Option 2): Kerala's dance-drama form, but not associated with these particular older names.

 

• Sattriya dance (Option 3): The classical dance of Assam, associated with Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras), unrelated to these terms.

question: Which metal ion released from tannery industry causes acute water pollution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cr.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The tannery (leather-processing) industry widely uses chromium salts (especially chromium sulphate) in the chrome tanning process to convert raw animal hides into leather. (क्रोमियम — चमड़ा उद्योग जल प्रदूषण)

 

• Effluents from tanneries, if untreated, discharge hexavalent chromium (Cr VI), a highly toxic and carcinogenic form, into water bodies, causing acute and chronic water pollution.

 

• Chromium contamination affects aquatic life and can enter the food chain and groundwater, posing serious health hazards to humans, including skin and respiratory problems.

 

• India has significant tannery clusters (e.g., in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu), where chromium pollution of rivers like the Ganga has been a major environmental concern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Arsenic (As) contamination in India is more commonly associated with groundwater in the Gangetic plains (West Bengal, Bihar), from geogenic sources, not tanneries.

 

• The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) regulates permissible chromium discharge limits from tanneries under environmental protection laws.

 

NOTE

 

• Mg (Option 1): Magnesium is not the pollutant typically associated with tannery effluent.

 

• As (Option 2): Arsenic pollution is linked to natural groundwater contamination, not primarily to tanneries.

 

• Zn (Option 4): Zinc is not the characteristic pollutant of the tanning process; chromium is.

question: The plan that mainly aims to coordinate both, private and public investment and output plans through targets is called__________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is indicative planning.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indicative planning is a form of economic planning where the government sets broad targets and provides indicative signals/guidance to coordinate both private and public sector investment and output plans, without making compliance mandatory for the private sector. (सांकेतिक नियोजन — निजी और सार्वजनिक निवेश का समन्वय)

 

• Unlike centralised/imperative planning, indicative planning relies on incentives, information-sharing and persuasion rather than direct control, allowing market forces to still operate.

 

• India adopted elements of indicative planning especially from the Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-97) onwards, after the 1991 economic liberalisation, moving away from the earlier more centralised Soviet-style approach.

 

• The government still sets targets for key macroeconomic and sectoral indicators, which serve as a coordinating device for both public and private investment decisions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• France was one of the pioneers of indicative planning in the mid-20th century.

 

• A rolling plan is a plan formulated every year, with targets revised annually, as attempted in India during 1978-80.

 

NOTE

 

• rolling plan (Option 2): Refers to a plan revised annually rather than one aimed specifically at coordinating public-private investment via targets.

 

• decentralised planning (Option 3): Refers to planning done at the state/local/panchayat level, not this coordination mechanism.

 

• centralised planning (Option 4): Involves the state directly controlling and mandating investment and production decisions, the opposite of the indicative, coordination-based approach described.

solution_text:
The correct answer is R Praggnanandhaa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian chess Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa defeated the then world number one Magnus Carlsen during the FTX Crypto Cup 2022 and went on to finish as the runner-up of the tournament. (आर प्रज्ञानानंदा — मैग्नस कार्लसन को हराया)

 

• This win made global headlines as a major breakthrough for the young Indian prodigy against the reigning world chess champion at the time.

 

• Praggnanandhaa, born in 2005, is known for becoming one of the youngest Grandmasters in chess history.

 

• The FTX Crypto Cup 2022 was part of the Champions Chess Tour, an elite online rapid chess circuit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Praggnanandhaa later went on to defeat Carlsen again and reached the final of the FIDE World Cup 2023, further cementing his reputation as a top young talent.

 

• Viswanathan Anand, India's first Grandmaster and five-time World Chess Champion, has mentored several young Indian players including Praggnanandhaa through his WestBridge Anand Chess Academy (WACA).

 

NOTE

 

• Saket Myneni (Option 1): Not associated with this achievement; not a chess Grandmaster of comparable prominence in this event.

 

• Vishwanathan Anand (Option 2): A legendary Indian Grandmaster, but he was not the one who achieved this particular feat at the FTX Crypto Cup 2022.

 

• P Harikrishna (Option 4): A strong Indian Grandmaster, but not the player who defeated Carlsen and finished runner-up at this event.

question: In the estimation of national income, which of the following items will be subtracted from NNP at market price?
option_2: Net product taxes and net production taxes
solution_text:
The correct answer is Net indirect taxes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Income (NNP at Factor Cost) is derived from NNP at Market Price by subtracting Net Indirect Taxes (Indirect Taxes minus Subsidies): NNP at FC = NNP at MP - Net Indirect Taxes. (शुद्ध अप्रत्यक्ष कर — NNP बाजार मूल्य से राष्ट्रीय आय)

 

• Market price includes indirect taxes (like GST) which inflate the price above the actual factor cost, while subsidies reduce the price below factor cost; hence net indirect taxes must be removed to arrive at the true income earned by factors of production.

 

• National Income, by definition, refers to NNP at Factor Cost, representing the sum of factor incomes (rent, wages, interest, profit) earned by normal residents of a country.

 

• Depreciation, on the other hand, is subtracted from GNP (Gross National Product) to arrive at NNP (Net National Product), a separate step in the sequence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The full sequence is: GDP at MP -> GNP at MP (add net factor income from abroad) -> NNP at MP (subtract depreciation) -> NNP at FC/National Income (subtract net indirect taxes).

 

• Net indirect taxes = Indirect taxes - Subsidies.

 

NOTE

 

• Depreciation (Option 1): Subtracted from GNP, not from NNP at market price, to arrive at NNP.

 

• Net product taxes and net production taxes (Option 2): These together constitute net indirect taxes but are listed here as a distractor sub-classification rather than the standard aggregate term used for this step.

 

• Depreciation and net product taxes (Option 4): Incorrectly combines two separate steps of the national income computation.

question: Which type of surveillance is specifically aimed at identifying missing cases of disease?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sentinel surveillance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sentinel surveillance is a monitoring system where a limited network of selected reporting sites ("sentinel sites") is specifically used to detect cases of a disease that would otherwise go unreported/missed by the routine (passive) reporting system. (सेंटिनल निगरानी — छूटे हुए मामलों की पहचान)

 

• It is particularly useful for diseases where complete case reporting through general health systems is inadequate, providing more detailed and reliable data from selected high-quality reporting sites.

 

• Sentinel surveillance systems are commonly used for diseases like influenza, HIV and other high-priority conditions in public health programmes.

 

• It complements routine passive surveillance by filling gaps in disease case detection.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Passive surveillance relies on routine reporting from existing health facilities without active follow-up.

 

• Active surveillance involves health authorities regularly and proactively contacting healthcare providers to seek case information for a specific condition.

 

NOTE

 

• Overt surveillance (Option 1): Refers to monitoring done openly, with the knowledge of those being observed; not specifically about finding missed disease cases.

 

• Passive surveillance (Option 2): Relies on data as routinely reported, without a specific mechanism to catch unreported/missed cases.

 

• Active surveillance (Option 3): Involves regular direct contact with providers for reporting of known conditions, but the standard public-health definition used for identifying otherwise-missed cases is sentinel surveillance.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution protects monuments or a place of artistic or historical interest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 49.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 49 of the Indian Constitution, a Directive Principle of State Policy, obliges the State to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historic interest, declared by or under law made by Parliament to be of national importance, from spoliation, disfigurement, destruction, removal, disposal or export. (अनुच्छेद 49 — स्मारकों का संरक्षण)

 

• This provision underpins laws like the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958, which empowers the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to protect nationally important monuments.

 

• It reflects the constitutional commitment to preserving India's rich cultural and historical heritage.

 

• Being a DPSP, Article 49 is not directly enforceable in courts but guides state policy and legislation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 48 deals with organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry, including prohibition of cow slaughter.

 

• Article 51 deals with the promotion of international peace and security.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 48 (Option 1): Relates to agriculture and animal husbandry, not monument protection.

 

• Article 50 (Option 3): Relates to separation of the judiciary from the executive.

 

• Article 51 (Option 4): Relates to the promotion of international peace and security, unrelated to heritage protection.

question:
Identify the correct statement/s with respect to NABARD’s EShakti project.

i. The project aimed to digitise the financial and non-financial data of all the SHGs.

ii. The project aimed to bring awareness about Digital India among the farmers.

iii. This project was launched by NABARD in March 2015.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only i and iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NABARD's e-Shakti project was launched in March 2015 as a pilot to digitise the financial and non-financial data of Self-Help Groups (SHGs), creating a comprehensive, real-time database. (ई-शक्ति परियोजना — नाबार्ड, मार्च 2015)

 

• Statement i is correct: The core objective of e-Shakti is the digitisation of SHG bookkeeping and member/group data to improve transparency and credit-linkage assessment by banks.

 

• Statement iii is correct: The project was indeed launched by NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) in March 2015, initially as a pilot in select districts.

 

• Statement ii is incorrect: e-Shakti's objective is specifically about SHG data digitisation and financial inclusion, not general "Digital India" awareness among farmers, which is a separate, broader government initiative.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• e-Shakti helps banks assess the creditworthiness of SHGs more efficiently, supporting easier and faster credit linkage.

 

• NABARD, established in 1982, is India's apex development bank for agriculture and rural development.

 

NOTE

 

• Only ii (Option 1): Incorrect, since statement ii is not a genuine objective of e-Shakti, and this option also omits the correct statements i and iii.

 

• Only i and ii (Option 3): Incorrectly includes the false statement ii while correctly including i, but wrongly excludes the correct statement iii.

 

• Only ii and iii (Option 4): Incorrectly includes the false statement ii and excludes the correct statement i.

question: Proportional taxes would help to reduce the autonomous expenditure multiplier because _______.
option_2: MPC does not have any role in it
solution_text:
The correct answer is taxes reduce the MPC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The autonomous expenditure multiplier is given by k = 1 / (1 - MPC), where MPC (Marginal Propensity to Consume) out of national income determines how strongly an initial change in autonomous spending gets multiplied. (गुणक — कर, सीमांत उपभोग प्रवृत्ति)

 

• When a proportional tax is introduced, only a fraction of any additional income is left as disposable income for households to spend, so the effective MPC out of total income (as opposed to disposable income) falls.

 

• Since a lower effective MPC reduces the value of the multiplier k = 1/(1-MPC), the introduction of proportional taxes reduces the size of the autonomous expenditure multiplier.

 

• This is a standard result in Keynesian macroeconomics: taxes act as an automatic stabiliser, dampening the multiplier effect of changes in autonomous spending.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• With proportional income tax at rate t, the multiplier becomes k = 1 / [1 - MPC(1-t)], which is smaller than the multiplier without taxes.

 

• Automatic stabilisers like proportional/progressive taxes help smooth out fluctuations in national income over the business cycle.

 

NOTE

 

• taxes increase the MPC (Option 1): Incorrect; taxes reduce the effective MPC out of total income, not increase it.

 

• MPC does not have any role in it (Option 2): Incorrect; MPC is central to the multiplier formula and to how taxes affect it.

 

• taxes and MPC become equal (Option 3): This is not a meaningful or correct economic relationship.

question: Who was the Chief guest on 26th January 2023 Republic Day Parade?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abdel Fattah El Sisi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Abdel Fattah El Sisi, the President of Egypt, was the Chief Guest at India's 74th Republic Day Parade on 26th January 2023. (अब्देल फतह अल-सिसी — मिस्र के राष्ट्रपति, गणतंत्र दिवस 2023 मुख्य अतिथि)

 

• This was a historic occasion as it marked the first time an Egyptian President was the Chief Guest at India's Republic Day celebrations.

 

• For the first time, a contingent of the Egyptian armed forces also took part in the Republic Day parade, reflecting deepening India-Egypt strategic ties.

 

• His visit also saw both countries elevate their relationship to a "Strategic Partnership".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Republic Day Chief Guest tradition dates back to 1950, when Indonesian President Sukarno was the first Chief Guest.

 

• India did not have a Chief Guest at Republic Day 2021 and 2022 due to the COVID-19 pandemic (an intended UK PM visit for 2021 was cancelled).

 

NOTE

 

• Cyril Ramaphosa (Option 1): President of South Africa; he was the Chief Guest at India's Republic Day in 2019, not 2023.

 

• Shinzo Abe (Option 2): Former Prime Minister of Japan; he was Chief Guest at India's Republic Day in 2014, and had passed away in 2022, before this event.

 

• Jair Bolsonaro (Option 3): Former President of Brazil; he was Chief Guest at India's Republic Day in 2020, not 2023.
